verdict.line: You lose if she lands Harsh Lesson and tether chains near a wall before level 6; you win if you farm Q stacks clean and carry the fight into Trinity Force/Frozen Heart territory.

brief.thesis: Illaoi's whole kit is built to force extended fights on terrain: Q (Tentacle Smash) empowers wall-spawned Tentacles, W (Harsh Lesson) leaps you into their swing range, and E (Test of Spirit) threatens to turn you into a Vessel that spawns more of them against you. Nasus's kit rewards the opposite: quiet farming for Q stacks and a slow, patient scale. The 47.8% head-to-head over 115 games is the early all-in window she owns before your Siphoning Strike hits real damage and you finish a core item.

theirWindow.when: E (Test of Spirit) cooldown is up
theirWindow.what: She'll tether you near a wall. Hug the spirit instead of running, since getting too far from it or letting it die turns you into a Vessel that spawns Tentacles against you.

yourWindow.when: Your W and stacked Q are ready
yourWindow.what: Land Wither before you extend; the decelerating slow cuts the attack speed she needs to proc tentacle swings, then finish the trade with a high-stack Siphoning Strike for the kill threat.

powerCurve.note: Harsh Lesson leap wins early poke trades
Tentacles near walls punish forced trades
Both ults online, Wither offsets her Leap
Q stacks and items start closing gap
Stacked Q and core items favor Nasus

start.why: The sustain and passive block absorb the chip from her early Tentacle Smash and Harsh Lesson pokes while Soul Eater is still weak, letting you hold the farm trade.

boots.why: Lower cooldowns put Wither and Spirit Fire up more often, which is what actually controls her Tentacle procs and leap timing, not raw armor.

core.why: The on-hit proc and attack speed turn stacked Siphoning Strikes into real burst the moment you start winning trades.
Armor and the attack speed slow directly blunt her Tentacle and auto damage in extended fights near walls.
Stacks with Soul Eater lifesteal and Fury of the Sands' health drain so sustained trades swing back in your favor.

situational.when: she's stacking lifesteal or heavy auto damage and you need grievous wounds to cut her sustain
the early Tentacle chip near walls is too punishing and you need armor and health on your first back
you need the extra slow zone to control Vessels and Tentacles spawned off her E

runes.keystoneWhy: The free sustain and movement speed let you manage distance from her E tether and dodge Harsh Lesson leaps, which is the single biggest survival skill in this lane.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is the highest-winrate combo in these games (54.3%). Flash dodges the Harsh Lesson leap or an E tether, and Teleport resets you after a bad trade or lets you answer a tentacle-wall skirmish elsewhere on the map.

playing.title: Farm Q, don't trade blind
playing.detail: Last-hit with Siphoning Strike to stack it rather than contesting her auto trades; every stack you bank is damage she can't out-scale later.

playing.title: Hug the spirit, don't flee it
playing.detail: If her E (Test of Spirit) lands on you, staying near the spirit matters more than killing it or running, since getting too far or letting it die makes you a Vessel that spawns Tentacles against you.

playing.title: Stay off the walls
playing.detail: Standing near impassible terrain lets her W (Harsh Lesson) trigger nearby Tentacles to swing at you too, on top of whatever Vessels or Spirits from her E are already feeding them.

playing.title: Wither before you commit
playing.detail: Cast W on her before extending into any trade; the decelerating slow strips the attack speed her Tentacle procs and autos depend on.

playing.title: Drop Spirit Fire on her dive
playing.detail: Zone with E the moment she leaps in with W; the armor shred makes every follow-up Tentacle and auto hit harder on her, not you.

playing.title: Save Fury of the Sands for forced fights
playing.detail: Hold R until she's committed to an all-in or a Leap of Faith; the health drain only becomes real damage in fights that actually last.

playing.title: Play the long game if you're losing lane
playing.detail: The matchup sits at 47.8% over 115 games, so if she's winning early skirmishes, stop forcing even trades and out-scale through farm and Teleport-enabled side lane pressure instead.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade timing are my own read of the matchup, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Illaoi’s (E) while laning. Focus on farming with [Q] to gain stacks and heal, and always manage your distance to avoid Illaoi’s skills.
